description: CalEITC and the Young Child Tax Credit are California tax-return credits. Use the forms and limits for the year you are filing.
introduction: CalEITC and the Young Child Tax Credit are California tax-return credits. Use the forms and limits for the year you are filing.

sections.who: For 2025, CalEITC requires qualifying earned income up to $32,900, a qualifying age or child, California residency and valid SSNs or ITINs, with filing-status and dependency rules. YCTC requires an eligible child under six at year-end.
sections.get: The refund or tax reduction depends on income and family circumstances. The published 2025 maximums are up to $3,756 for CalEITC and $1,189 for YCTC; they are not guaranteed awards.
sections.docs: Keep wages/self-employment records, taxpayer and child IDs, residency and qualifying-child information. For YCTC with zero or negative earned income, check its additional wage and loss rules.
sections.apply:
1. Calculate eligibility using FTB’s tax-year guidance.

  2. Complete FTB 3514 and include it with the California return. Free CalFile or VITA help may be available. Use prior-year forms for a prior-year claim.
sections.after: Keep the return and credit worksheet. Respond to FTB verification requests using the instructions in its notice.
sections.sources:
Application and program details: 2025 eligibility and credit amounts, 2025 FTB 3514 and YCTC instructions.

Historical screenshots and background: USA Assistance. Screenshots may show an earlier application interface.

faqs: Yes, when the remaining requirements are met.
Must a YCTC applicant always have positive earned income?
No. Zero or negative income can qualify under additional rules.
Does having a child under six guarantee YCTC?
No. The other qualifying-child and credit conditions still apply.
Are the maximum amounts the same every year?
No. Use the guidance for the return’s tax year.
